title: Woodcore form
description: templates/forms/<id>/form.json -- the file that makes a folder a form, the look of a project's three documents (calc/forms.py): a `template.typ` defining `#let template(doc, lang:, region:)`, a `title.typ` defining `#let title-page(document:)` and the assets they use (a logo). A form is the layout alone -- fonts, sizes, margins, headings, the page's furniture, the title page's layout -- and holds no project data. Applying a form copies the folder into the project's `Template/` (its form.json rewritten with the form's id and place, title.typ going to the top of the project instead) and archives what was there. Three places: builtin (`templates/forms/`, read only), user and shared (`forms/` inside the engineer's or the office's folder of templates). A form the engineer or the office saved from a project usually names itself in the one language it is written in.

schema_version.description: -- pinned: a form written at another version is refused rather than read as this one.

format.description: What this file is, so a form.json that is something else is refused by name.

id.description: Only in the form.json copied into a project's `Template/`: the folder name of the form it was made from (`bfh`, `Holzbau`), so the project says which form it is written in.

place.description: Only in the form.json copied into a project's `Template/`: the place the form came from.

name.description: The form's name as a list shows it, per language: at least one.

description.description: What the form is for, per language. Optional.
